claims.text: Replacing TOR-TILD's conventional EAM reference with a deep-learning potential trained on ab initio data is the proposed intervention.
The training data should comprehensively sample both solid and high-temperature liquid configurations.
TOR-TILD's EAM references inadequately represent the range of configurations in high-temperature HEA liquids.
A deep-learning potential can capture the many-body atomic interactions present across the broad configurational space of high-temperature solid and liquid HEAs.
The trained potential will accurately reproduce DFT forces and energies for high-temperature solid and liquid HEA configurations.
Training on high-temperature DFT configurations will make the deep-learning potential represent the diverse atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid better than an EAM reference.
The improved representation will increase reference–target phase-space overlap.
Increasing reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce errors or mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will decrease by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The deep-learning reference will yield more accurate melting temperatures and free-energy differences.
The proposed method is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic multicomponent HEAs at 2500–4000 K.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid states near melting.
Improvement depends on sufficiently comprehensive training coverage of solid and liquid states within the specified temperature and composition ranges.
Systems outside the training domain or with drastically different bonding characteristics may not show the same improvement.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on ab initio training-data coverage and deep-learning hyperparameter optimization.
